summary: W2-UI-SHELL wave 2 is done. All 19 brief IDs, the 6 FX-UI round-1 leftovers and the PM's monitor-socket request are in findings: 16 fixed (2 by verification only) and 3 partially fixed, plus the 6 leftovers and the socket lifecycle fixed (C1-trader-ux-11 and -18: the rest is in other owners' files; C1-trader-ux-13: two socket chips need PR-CHIP1/2). Main changes: per-page error boundaries plus a no-stack global-error card and K1 error reports; no bootstrap gate (the stock list for EQS only); the reconnected event that reloads failed pages; one status chrome in the app; header row 1 that never overflows; UPDATE DATA with a confirmation; honest closed-market / LINK DOWN chips; K3 strip counter-zoom; K4 ?sym= and NEW WINDOW; type-to-GO, Esc and real page history; boot preload of the first page; finite animations; PIPE mounted on demand; an isolated header clock; one shared eco-calendar request. I adopted and reviewed the duplicate's socket lifecycle (AppContext, monitorLifecycle, ws.check). It is correct and minimal, and I extended ws.check to 66 checks with a negative control for the wsManager defect, whose fix is PR-WS1. Patch requests: PR-WS1 (wsManager), PR-OPS1 (netpolicy expected deltas) and PR-CHIP1/2 (socket chips), all validated on scratch trees. Gates: tsc clean; desktop 222, prefs 160, platform 120, alerts 18, ws 66, ui/scripts 26; pytest desktop contract + harness 104. Browser: 13/13 sections in Chromium AND WebKit through w2shell_server, with 0 live socket accepts. ui_audit: Chromium 39/42 PASS, WebKit 38/42 PASS. Every failure except one is an expected POST refused by --block-mutations: ostrategy POST /api/options/strategy/analyze, discovery POST /api/alpha/scan, mcxgold POST /api/mcx/ticket (403, both engines). The exception is one transient WebKit 502 on commodity GET /api/commodity/gold-preopen/log?threshold=300. It is not reproducible: a direct GET gives 200, every ui-api log line for it is 200, and a commodity re-audit in WebKit gives 1/1 PASS. 0 page errors. The wrapper counted 84 local monitor sockets (one per page load), 84 closed, all with code 1000. One live :8010 monitor accept in that window came from the installed SuryaDhana.app (system WebKit Networking pid 42761), not from the audit. Disclosure: one run of mine (14:56-14:58), before I fixed the harness, opened live monitor sockets (see open_issues).

findings.what_changed: New components/shell/TabErrorBoundary.tsx wraps each of the 42 pages, keyed by page id. The fallback is a terminal-styled '<CODE> FAILED TO RENDER' panel with RETRY, a DETAILS disclosure (message and stacks, hidden by default) and COPY. The header, strip, tape, page strip, footer, GO bar and navigation stay mounted. There are variants for the header ('bar' with RETRY), the stock window ('modal' with CLOSE, Esc works too) and the GO bar / news dock ('silent'). The boundary resets on page change, on RETRY and on the 'suryadhana:reconnected' event. A ChunkLoadError gets the guarded reload instead of the panel. app/global-error.tsx is the last-resort card: no raw stack by default (behind a disclosure), with RELOAD. ErrorCatcher's full overlay is now behind `next dev` or localStorage 'suryadhana.debug.errors'='1'. Users see a compact '⚠ N UI ERROR(S)' footer chip instead (list, COPY DETAILS, CLEAR).

Limits: dedup per fingerprint, a per-minute and a per-page cap, clipped fields (well under 8 KB), control characters stripped, url = path+query only. QA contexts with prefs mode 'readonly' never POST, so live audits stay GET-only. The server route is W2-API's services/ui-api/routers/client_errors.py (present in the repo).

findings.what_changed: On LINK DOWN -> LINK UP, PlatformShell dispatches 'suryadhana:reconnected' {outageMs} and bumps ShellState.reconnects. app/page.tsx then reloads the active page and an open stock window, but only when the page's visible text shows a failed load or a crashed render (lib/reconnect.ts needsReloadAfterOutage: axios, WebKit 'Load failed', Chromium 'Failed to fetch', HTTP 5xx, the boundary text). Healthy pages keep their state. While LINK DOWN the page is dimmed under an in-page notice ('LINK DOWN since HH:MM IST · the panels below show the last data received…'). The banner copy now promises only what is true: 'panels show the last data received · failed pages reload when the link is back'. The footer reads OFFLINE · LINK DOWN.

The ENRICH completion refresh reloads those only if they were loaded. A real ui-api outage is the connection banner's job, so the misleading 'Backend unreachable' gate diagnosis is gone. What EQS and OVRV show is unchanged.

patch_requests.why: PR-WS1 (wsManager, from the PM's socket-lifecycle request). A superseded socket's late close event (disconnect() closed it, then a reconnect replaced it, e.g. pagehide -> pageshow or a remount) runs the shared onclose. That stops the LIVE socket's 25 s heartbeat, emits status false, and, when the old socket was closed while CONNECTING (close code 1006), schedules a spurious reconnect that doubles the backoff. The fix ignores close events of any socket that is no longer this.ws. A server drop of the live socket is unchanged. Verified: the patched scratch tree is tsc clean and ws.check 66/66 (section 7 enforces heartbeat kept and no spurious reconnect). The unpatched repo reproduces both defects (section 7 negative control). After it lands, ws.check.ts switches to enforcing automatically (it detects the guard). I do not think wsManager.ts should move to me: the fix is this one guard.

Wave 2 removed three page-independent requests from the pages that do not show their data: the 1,500-stock list (EQS only, C1-trader-ux-03), the enrichment status (OVRV only) and the PipelineStudio polls (PIPE only, C2-performance-06). parity.py against an older build (:3000 or a pre-wave-2 release) would report 'API request set differs' on almost every page. open_issues: Live sockets before the fix to my harness (my responsibility). Between 14:56 and 14:58 my Chromium run (C,K,P,I) went through the STOCK scratch relay on :8093, which relays /api/monitor/ws/monitor to live :8010. Its P negative control (--live) also loaded 5 pages directly from :8010. Those page loads opened live monitor sockets. The twin's 15:00 WebKit run through :8096 did the same. Since 15:05 every browser run has used w2shell_server, and the harness now mocks the socket in the browser and refuses a base without /__qa/ws: 0 live accepts.

For W2-API (hang root cause). The live ui-api log since the 14:48 restart (pid 70501) shows 177 'WebSocket /api/monitor/ws/monitor [accepted]' / 'connection open' lines and 0 'connection closed' lines. That is the same pattern as the hang, although lsof shows only a handful of established :8010 connections, so TCP does close. Either the handler never returns after a client disconnect or the close is not logged. The UI side now closes with 1000 on pagehide and unmount (verified end to end).
